package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via bundling/drive-by downloads, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The Fireball malware is a browser hijacker with remote control capabilities, designed to infect millions of machines worldwide. It manipulates browser settings, injects advertisements, and can execute arbitrary code on infected systems, enabling large-scale ad fraud and potentially more severe attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon browser launch or system startup)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into browser process or installed as a browser extension/add-on

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies browser settings to set a malicious homepage and search engine, injects advertisements into web pages, and checks for remote commands to execute, resulting in browser hijacking, ad fraud, and potential remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code forcibly changes browser settings and injects ads without user consent, and includes a remote command execution capability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal browser extensions or software should not change user settings or execute arbitrary remote code without explicit user permission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise browser management tools may set homepage/search engine, but only with user or admin consent and without ad injection or remote code execution.

attack_chain.action: Malware is delivered to the victim's machine via software bundling or drive-by download.
attack_chain.leads_to: Installation and persistence on the system

attack_chain.action: On system startup or browser launch, the malware executes and hijacks browser settings, injects ads, and establishes remote control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing ad fraud and potential remote code execution

attack_chain.action: Malware receives and executes remote commands, potentially downloading further payloads or exfiltrating data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the system or further monetization

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized modification of browser homepage and search engine settings
Injection of advertisements into web pages outside of normal ad networks
Browser extension or process making remote command-and-control requests
file_indicators: Unexpected changes to browser configuration files (e.g., prefs.js for Firefox, registry for IE/Edge/Chrome)
Presence of files or processes with names mimicking legitimate browser components
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Fireball C2 domains or ad fraud infrastructure
Frequent HTTP requests to domains set as new homepage/search engine
Unusual traffic patterns from browser processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to browser settings, unexpected browser extensions, and outbound network connections to suspicious domains. Use endpoint protection to detect browser hijacking behaviors and remote code execution attempts. Correlate browser configuration changes with process creation and network activity to identify malicious patterns.
